 SRI N.K.HARISH, ADVOCATE FOR R2)
 THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S 482 OF CR.P.C. PRAYING TO QUASH THE COMPLAINT DATED 13.03.2019 AND FIR FILED IN CR.NO.173/2019 PENDING ON THE FILE OF VII ADDL. C.M.M.,
BENGALURU, FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 120(B), 419, 420, 468,
465, 471, 474 AND 467 OF IPC.
 THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA  ORAL ORDER

The petitioner-accused in Cr.No.173/2019 of Rajagopal Nagara Police Station registered for the offences punishable under Section 120B, 419, 420, 468, 465, 471, 474 and 467 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC') is before this Court seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against him.
2. Heard Sri.Sharath.S.Gowda, learned counsel for petitioner, Smt.K.P.Yashodha, learned HCGP for respondent No.1 and Sri.N.K.Harish, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the material on record.

Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner is arrayed as accused No.1 in the above criminal proceedings initiated on the basis of the first information lodged by respondent No.2 for the above said offences.

Learned counsel submits that respondent No.2 said to have purchased site No.17 under the registered sale deed dated 25.03.2006 from general power of attorney holder by name Sri.Venkatesh, representing the original owner.

In fact the said Venkatesh is none other than the husband of respondent No.2.
4.
Learned counsel submits that the original owner executed GPA dated 15.06.1985 along with affidavit and the said GPA is coupled with interest as the GPA holder had paid Rs.22,000/- in favour of owner.

Pursuant to the GPA dated 15.06.1985, he has executed the registered sale deed dated 07.12.2018 in respect of the very site for valuable consideration of Rs.30,00,000/- which was paid through Cheques.

Learned counsel submits that paper publication was published in the daily newspaper inviting the objections from public for purchasing the site and no NC: 2024:KHC:32455 objections were received and thereafter, petitioner No.1 purchased the property under the sale deed.

Basavaraju H M vs State By on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192231440/
2 5.

entities.text: Basavaraju H M vs State By on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that conduct of petitioner discloses that he had no intention to commit cheating as otherwise he would not have published the public notice before purchase of the property and he would not have paid the consideration amount through Cheques.
6. Learned counsel submits that legal representatives of original owners have filed the suit O.S.No.9223/2019, wherein, the petitioner and respondent No.2 were defendants.

During the pendency of the suit, legal representatives of original owners executed registered confirmation deed dated 25.01.2019 confirming execution of sale deed dated 07.12.2018 and later name of petitioner No.1 was deleted from the suit.

However, respondent No.2 has filed counter claim in the said suit, to the effect that the sale deed executed in favour of petitioner is null and void and the said counter claim was filed in the absence of petitioner and the said judgment is challenged before this Court in R.F.A.No.1689/2024, the NC: 2024:KHC:32455 same is pending for consideration.

Therefore,
learned counsel submits that the dispute between the parties is purely civil in nature and the facts and circumstances of the case disclose that there was no intention on the part of the petitioner to commit cheating at the inception which is the basic requirement of law to invoke Section 420 of IPC.

He has placed reliance on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Vijay Kumar Ghai and Others V/s State of West Bengal and Others1 AIR Online 2022 SC 380 in support of his contention and therefore prays for allowing the petition.
7.

entities.text: Vijay Kumar Ghai and Others V/s State of West Bengal and Others1 AIR Online 2022 SC 380
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per Contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 opposing the petition submitted that respondent No.2 is the original purchaser of the site in question under registered sale deed dated 25.03.2006 through the general power of attorney holder.

Thereafter this petitioner managed to get the GPA in the name of One Venkatesh and got the sale deed executed through him AIR Online 2022 SC 380 NC: 2024:KHC:32455 because the first GPA holder was also by name Venkatesh and the same was with an intention to commit cheating.
8. Learned counsel submits that counter claim in O.S.No.9223/2019 is decreed and therefore the contention of respondent No.2 is further strengthened.
Under such circumstances the petition is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, prays for dismissal of petition.
9. Learned HCGP submitted that except registering the FIR, there is no further investigation in the matter, since interim stay is granted by this Court.
Hence, she pray for passing appropriate orders.

10. In view of the rival contention urged by learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
" Whether this petitioner has made out any ground to allow this petition and to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against him?"
NC: 2024:KHC:32455 11.

My answer to the above point is in the ' affirmative ' for the following:
REASONS Basavaraju H M vs State By on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192231440/
3 12.

entities.text: REASONS Basavaraju H M vs State By on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The admitted facts of the case of respondent No.2 is that, she had purchased site No.17 through GPA holder one Venkatesh who incidentally is her husband, under the sale deed dated 25.03.2006.
It is stated that the original owners have executed the GPA in favour of her husband on 06.10.1986.

It is the contention of the petitioner that the original owners have executed the GPA in favor of one Venkatesh on 15.06.1985 after accepting an amount of Rs.22,000/- and therefore the said GPA is coupled with interest.

The GPA holder had executed the registered sale deed in favour of the petitioner on 07.12.2018 after accepting the valuable consideration of Rs.30,00,000/- which was paid through Cheques and copies of the sale deed are produced for perusal.

13. The undisputed fact of the case is that the legal representatives of the original owner have filed the suit in NC: 2024:KHC:32455 O.S.No.9223/2019 seeking partition and separate possession of various properties, including the site bearing No.17.
The petitioner and respondent No.2 are the defendants in the said suit.
Admittedly, the name of petitioner came to be deleted after the legal representatives of the original owner executed registered confirmation deed, confirming execution of sale deed dated 07.12.2018.

However, it is stated that respondent No.2 being one of the defendant in the suit filed a counter claim and the said counter claim is said to have been decreed in the absence of the petitioner which is challenged before this Court in R.F.A.No.1689/2024, which is pending consideration and an order of stay is granted for the decree passed by the Trial Court.
14.

Learned counsel for petitioner produced Annexure-J that is copy of the paper publication to contend that before proceeding to get the sale deed dated 07.12.2018 executed through the GPA holder, a public notice was issued in Kannada Daily Newspaper inviting the general public to have their objections if any, with regard NC: 2024:KHC:32455 to the schedule property.
I find considerable force in the contention of learned counsel for petitioner that if the petitioner was having an intention to cheat, he would not have issued public notice in the newspaper.

15. Learned counsel for the petitioner placed reliance on the decision Vijay Kumar Ghai (supra),
wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court referring to its earlier decision in Vesa Holdings PVt. Ltd., and Anr. V/s State of Kerala and Others2 and extracted paragraph No.13 to hold that the real test is whether allegations in the complaint disclose the criminal offence of cheating or not.

entities.text: Anr. V/s State of Kerala and Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is made clear that at the very inception there has to be an intention on behalf of the accused to cheat, which is a condition precedent for an offence under Section 420 of IPC.
16.
On going through these facts, I am of the opinion that there are no prima facie materials against the petitioner.
It is for the parties to settle their disputes (2015) 8 SCC 293 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:32455 before the Civil Court by leading evidence in support of their contention.
I do not find any prima facie material to attract penal provisions against the petitioner.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioner is liable to be quashed as otherwise it amounts to abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I answered point as 'affirmative' and proceed to pass the following:
Basavaraju H M vs State By on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192231440/
4 ORDER i) The petition is allowed.

In view of disposal of the criminal petition, pending I.A.No.1/2022 does not survive for consideration.
